title: Choosing repertoire and pacing
summary: Carter says he chose songs he liked and thought about pacing in a program.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Let me ask something else, too, about what we might just put under the heading of 'repertoire'. What factors at various times in your career -- let's perhaps limit it to the question of your jazz work or what we'll call your jazz work, as unhappy as you are with that term, but it doesn't matter ...
Well, I'm not really unhappy with it. I just find it very limiting, yeah ...

But lacking a better term, at various stages of your career, how did you go about choosing a repertoire? That is, the music which was going to appear under your own name? I'm not talking about for hire work you did for other people -- but in your own bands, or -- especially in your own bands, what factors would have guided your choice of a repertoire, that is, the circumstances, or just what kinds of judgments?
You mean the sounds that I would select or something that I would write?
Well, both. I'm thinking more of a larger body of material that you put together, say, in a single evening, or over a certain period of time.
Just a song I would like, you know. I mean, you want to know how I -- on the basis of what would I choose a song I would like, or ...
Yeah ... or how you put together a body of material, what considerations? I mean, fast, slow?
Oh, you mean in a program?
Uh huh, in effect. Well, naturally, I think it would -- I would take in to consideration the matter
of pacing, you know, which I think is always something we think of in programming something -- one thing too similar doesn't follow another thing, you know.
